Rule text is draft copy (Krogering from design, the rest standard rules adapted to each summary). Verify against the real house rules. `covingtonOriginal` is a placeholder flag set only on Krogering.

games.name: Five-Card Stud
games.summary: One card down, four up, with a bet after every card. No draws and no community cards.

deal: Everyone antes. One card down and one card up.
High card showing bets first. Bet.
Third card up. Highest hand showing bets first. Bet.
Fourth card up. Bet.
Fifth card up. Last bet, then everyone still in turns over their hole card. Best five cards wins.
detail.houseNotes: No wild cards and no draws. If two players tie for the high hand showing, the one closest to the dealer's left bets first. Fold your hole card face down. Nobody gets to see it.

games.name: Seven-Card Stud
games.summary: Two down, four up, one down. Five rounds of betting and your best five of seven plays.

deal: Everyone antes. Two down, one up. Lowest card showing has to open. Bet.
Fourth, fifth and sixth cards come up with a bet after each. Highest hand showing bets first.
Seventh card down. Last bet.
Best five of your seven cards wins.
detail.houseNotes: With eight players the deck can run out before the last card. If there aren't enough cards for everyone on the last round, the dealer turns one card up in the middle and everybody uses it.

games.name: Criss Cross
games.summary: Five cards in the middle laid out in a cross. Use the row or the column, not both.
games.rankReason: four arms of the cross, crossed at the middle

deal: Everyone antes. Four cards down to each player. Bet.
Deal five cards face down in the middle in a cross: a row of three and a column of three that share the center card.
Turn over the two ends of the row. Bet.
Turn over the two ends of the column. Bet.
Turn over the middle card last. Last bet.
Make your best five cards from your four plus either the row or the column. You can't use cards from both.
detail.houseNotes: The middle card is part of both lines, but you only get to play one line. Some nights the middle card is wild, along with every card of that rank. The dealer has to say so before dealing.

games.name: Krogering
games.summary: Seven-card stud, but your lowest down card is wild, along with every card of that rank in your hand. Named after the guy who kept dealing it.

detail.summary: Seven-card stud where your lowest down card is wild, and so is every other card of that rank in your hand. If your last down card is lower, that becomes your wild card instead.
deal: Two down, then one up. Bet.
Three more up, a bet after each.
Last card down. Final bet.
Name your low hole card at showdown, not before. Best five of seven takes it.
detail.houseNotes: Aces are high, so an ace in the hole is never wild. Say what your wild card is before the hands are read, or your hand plays as dealt.

games.rankReason: the deuce, lowest card is wild

games.name: Chase the Queen
games.summary: When a queen is dealt face up, the next face-up card is wild for everyone. Another queen changes it.

deal: Everyone antes. Two down, one up. Bet.
Three more cards up with a bet after each.
When a queen is dealt face up, the next card dealt face up to anyone becomes wild, along with every card of that rank.
If another queen comes up, the old wild card is dead and the card after the new queen is wild. If a queen is the last face-up card dealt, only queens are wild.
Seventh card down. It doesn't change the wild card. Last bet, best five of seven wins.
detail.houseNotes: Queens are always wild. Only face-up queens change the wild card, so a queen in the hole doesn't count for that.

games.name: Screw Your Neighbor
games.summary: One card each and three lives. Keep your card or trade it to the left. Low card loses a life, and nobody can take a king.
games.rankReason: a king in hand cannot be taken

deal: Everyone puts one chip in the pot and keeps three in front of them as lives. One card each, face down. Aces are low.
The player left of the dealer goes first: keep your card, or trade it face down with the player on your left.
If you have a king, turn it face up. Nobody can trade with you, and the player who tried has to keep their card.
The dealer goes last and can trade with the top card of the deck instead. If that card is a king, the dealer keeps their own card.
Everyone turns their card over. Lowest card loses a life. If there's a tie for lowest, they all lose one.
When your chips are gone you're out. Last player with a chip left wins the pot.
detail.houseNotes: The deal moves left every hand. You can't turn down a trade. If the player on your right wants your card, they get it. You're allowed to try to talk them out of it.

games.name: Liar's Poker
games.summary: Bid on the digits in everyone's dollar bill serial numbers. Call a bluff and the bills go on the table.

deal: Everyone takes a dollar bill out of their own pocket and keeps the serial number hidden.
The first player bids a number of one digit across all the bills at the table, like "three sixes."
Each bid has to be higher than the last: more of any digit, or the same number of a higher digit. Ones are highest, then zeros, then nines down to twos.
Instead of raising, you can challenge. Once everyone else has challenged, put the bills face up and count.
If the bid is there, the bidder gets a dollar from each challenger. If it isn't, the bidder pays each of them a dollar.
detail.houseNotes: Play the bill you pulled out. No swapping it for a better one. The bidder's own bill counts. Whoever wins the round bids first on the next one.

games.name: Beat Charlie
games.summary: Charlie gets a hand in the middle and never bets or folds. If nobody beats Charlie, the pot carries over to the next deal.

deal: Everyone antes. Five cards down to each player and five face down to Charlie in the middle.
Bet. Then draw up to three cards. Charlie keeps what he was dealt.
Second bet. You can still fold.
Show your hands, then turn Charlie's over. The best hand at the table has to beat Charlie to win the pot.
If Charlie wins, nobody gets paid. Everyone antes again and the pot carries over to the next deal.
detail.houseNotes: Charlie wins ties. Charlie doesn't ante, doesn't fold and doesn't bluff.

games.name: In Between
games.summary: Bet that the next card lands between the two showing. Hit one of them and you pay double.

deal: Everyone antes into the pot.
On your turn, the dealer turns two cards face up. These are the posts.
Bet anywhere from one chip up to the whole pot that the next card will fall between them.
If it's in between, take your bet out of the pot. If it's outside, pay your bet into the pot. If it matches a post, pay double.
If the posts are a pair or next to each other, nothing can fall between them. Take two new cards or pass.
Keep going around the table until the pot is empty, then everyone antes again.
detail.houseNotes: If the first post is an ace, you call it high or low before the second card is turned. An ace on the second post is always high. Nobody can bet the whole pot the first time around the table.

games.name: Night Baseball
games.summary: Seven cards face down and nobody looks. Flip until you beat what's showing. Threes and nines are wild and a four gets you an extra card.

deal: Everyone antes. Seven cards face down to each player. Don't look at them.
The player left of the dealer turns over one card. Bet.
The next player turns over cards one at a time until they beat the best hand showing, then bet.
If you run out of cards before you beat it, you're out for the hand.
Threes and nines are wild. If you turn over a four, the dealer gives you an extra face-down card.
Keep going around until nobody can beat the best hand showing. Best five face-up cards wins.
detail.houseNotes: Only face-up cards count, wild cards included. Turn one card at a time and don't look at the rest of your cards.

games.name: Euchre
games.summary: A 24-card trick-taking game for two teams of two. Call trump and take at least three of the five tricks.

detail.summary: Partners sit across from each other and play with the nines through aces. The jack of trump is the highest card. The team that calls trump needs three of the five tricks, or they get euchred.
deal: Use the nines through aces, 24 cards. Partners sit across from each other. Deal five cards each in threes and twos, then turn the next card face up on the kitty.
Starting left of the dealer, each player can order it up, which makes that suit trump, or pass. If someone orders it up, the dealer picks up that card and discards one.
If all four pass, turn it face down. Go around again and anyone can name a different suit as trump or pass. If it gets back to the dealer, the dealer has to pick a suit.
Trump from high to low: jack of trump (right bower), the other jack of the same color (left bower), then ace, king, queen, ten, nine. The left bower counts as trump, not as its own suit.

The player left of the dealer leads. Follow suit if you can. If you can't, trump it or throw off any card. Highest trump wins the trick, otherwise the highest card of the suit led. Whoever wins leads next.
If the team that called trump takes three or four tricks, they get 1 point. All five is 2 points. If they take fewer than three they're euchred and the other team gets 2. First team to 10 wins.
detail.houseNotes: The player who calls trump can go alone. Their partner puts their cards down and sits out the hand. Taking all five tricks alone is worth 4 points, and three or four is still 1. The deal moves left each hand. Use the leftover fives and sixes to keep score.

games.rankReason: the right bower, jack of trump
